wiki_sources.section: Beikdugang - Founded by Zurkanreki merchants that were expelled from Tianlou, the fleet was celebrated with festivities as they exchanged naval supplies, maps, trinkets, bronze, and eventually coal. The fleet then proceeded to Tianlou.
wiki_sources.title: Treasure Fleet

rationale.colonization: The far north, Aelantir, and other transoceanic routes create long-distance management.
rationale.complexity: Routes, trade, allies, revolution, and artificery overlap across regions.
rationale.dark_story: War and the export of ideas carry risks, but terror rule is not the main theme.
rationale.difficulty: A cross-continental map and partner prerequisites are complex; this is not an in-game measurement.
rationale.diplomacy: The Lake Federation, overseas partners, and multi-continental agreements are central.
rationale.early_pressure: The opening trade port has resources, but Tianlou competition creates pressure.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: International artificer cooperation and the steam fleet are late-game focuses.
rationale.narrative_density: The story clearly shifts from port competition to global freedom and revolution.
rationale.tall_play: Ports, markets, constitutional institutions, and artificer production need sustained development.
rationale.trade_economy: Relic trade, ports, and fleets form the main economic loop.
rationale.warfare: The Tianlou contest and the later maritime revolution require war.

identity.appearance: A four-province Jiangyang merchant republic in 1444; Wang Ji rules, and Tianlou is its historic rival.
identity.formation_scope: The current Y15-specific maritime-trade and revolutionary missions do not require forming another Tag.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition only; racial and government bonuses and optional idea groups are excluded. Multiple candidates and conditions are listed separately and are not simultaneous additions; whether a formation accepts a new set depends on actual events, decisions, and player choice.

description.text: Our ancient forefathers came from the great trade fleets of the north, who stayed here and built our fair city with their bare hands. We are still seen as outsiders by many, and are far more open to new ideas that have been rejected by the rest of Yanshen for their radicality and strangeness.
description.text_en: Our ancient forefathers came from the great trade fleets of the north, who stayed here and built our fair city with their bare hands. We are still seen as outsiders by many, and are far more open to new ideas that have been rejected by the rest of Yanshen for their radicality and strangeness.

description.text: They come by every decade or so, mighty ships of the north with flags featuring the great rising sun of our ancestor's homeland. We remain one of their primary destinations, and benefit greatly from their honored patronage.
description.text_en: They come by every decade or so, mighty ships of the north with flags featuring the great rising sun of our ancestor's homeland. We remain one of their primary destinations, and benefit greatly from their honored patronage.

description.text:
Driven away by the war ravaging their homeland during the Daehonse Period, countless Gowon refugees flocked to our shores soon after the plot against Jaher succeeded, assisting us in defending against Tianlou in the aftermath. They have since settled into our city, building their own slice of home, Dajunshi, on her outskirts.

As well as bringing an exotic and lush culture to our people, their mastery with the bow and arrow has proved a powerful asset to our armies.

description.text: Our ships have always been legendary in these lands, based on the vessels of our progenitors and renowned for their durability and ease of maintenance.
description.text_en: Our ships have always been legendary in these lands, based on the vessels of our progenitors and renowned for their durability and ease of maintenance.

description.text: The hills north of Beikdugang are pockmarked with old and decaying fortifications built by a succession of conquerors and petty lords, we have a ready supply of material to pull from to repair our active bastions.
description.text_en: The hills north of Beikdugang are pockmarked with old and decaying fortifications built by a succession of conquerors and petty lords, we have a ready supply of material to pull from to repair our active bastions.

description.text: The city our forebears hailed from is known as Zhuhan to our people. While all of Yanshen marvels in the mystery and splendor of its treasure fleets, it holds a special place in our hearts. Rumoured to be a gleaming city of amber and jewels, where even the poorest citizen dresses in linens of silk and gold, we are proud to claim such distinguished heritage.

description.text: Our naval officer academy is one of the most prestigious in Yanshen, and frequently collaborates with the Abosrekodh academy back in Zhuhan. The gifted sailors and admirals that graduate from Nanxin are a powerful boon to our navy.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want quiet development at home and do not want long routes, allies, or multi-continental missions.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First contest Yanshen's land and sea trade routes, then maintain the Federation and overseas ports, and finally spread revolution while building an artificer fleet.
player_overview.overview: In 1444 Beikdugang is a merchant republic near the Yanshen estuary, locked in long competition with Tianlou. Establish yourself in land and sea trade, form transoceanic partnerships with the Lake Federation, explore the far north and overseas, and develop the relic market and ports. The later missions turn merchant routes into a network for rights and revolution, followed by international artificer cooperation and an expensive steam fleet. Its appeal is a map and political ideal that keep expanding; its cost is the long setup for intercontinental missions, fleets, and allies.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who like maritime trade, transcontinental diplomacy, liberal revolution, and the gradual fusion of artificer technology.
signature_features: Lake Federation cooperation runs through trade, constitutional reference, and overseas military affairs.
Overseas routes, the relic market, and international artificer research connect several continents.
Liberal-rights ideas move from domestic institutions to global revolution and a steam fleet.
player_overview.tagline: Set sail from an Eastern Haless trading port and build a free republic of fleets, equal partners, and artificer technology across the oceans.

reasons: Distinctive overseas trade and Lake Federation partnership
The relic market leads into global artificer research
Late global revolution and steam fleet create a major technological shift
warnings: Long routes and overseas prerequisites require patience
Older players reported ally or random-event delays; the new version must be judged from the actual scripts

positive_indicators: Uses constitutional principles to restrain power
Explicitly advocates personal rights for subjects and partners
Invests relics in international artificer research
values.rationale: Constitutionalism, equal subject-partner ideals, international knowledge-sharing, and rights propagation have positive evidence; exporting a global revolution may involve coercion, so restraint is lower than the other dimensions. A declaration alone does not prove that rights are implemented in every colony.
red_flags: Exporting global ideals carries a risk of military coercion
Overseas trade and relic allocation may prioritize merchant interests
